question: Three partners P, Q and R invest ₹1,000, ₹1,200 and ₹1,500, respectively, in a business. What should be the share of Q if the total profit is ₹666?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of investments = 1000 : 1200 : 1500 = 10 : 12 : 15.

Since the time period is identical, profit is distributed in the ratio of their investments.

Share of Q = [12 ÷ (10 + 12 + 15)] × Total Profit

Share of Q = (12 ÷ 37) × 666 = 12 × 18 = 216.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of P = ₹1000

Investment of Q = ₹1200

Investment of R = ₹1500

Total profit = ₹666

**Formula Used:**

When the investment time is the same for all partners, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio.

 Total Profit = ₹666 (37 parts)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Ratio of profits (P : Q : R) = 1000 : 1200 : 1500

⇒ Simplifying the ratio, we get 10 : 12 : 15

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 10 + 12 + 15 = 37 parts

⇒ Value of 37 parts = ₹666

⇒ Value of 1 part = 666 ÷ 37 = ₹18

⇒ Profit share of Q = 12 parts

⇒ Share of Q = 12 × 18 = ₹216

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Different Time Periods

If partners invest for different durations, their profit is shared in the ratio of the product of their Capital and Time (C₁ × T₁ : C₂ × T₂).

Working & Sleeping Partners

A working partner receives a fixed salary or a specific percentage of the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is distributed among all partners according to their investment ratios.

Compound Partnership

When a partner withdraws or adds money during the year, their capital is broken into time segments. The equivalent capital is calculated as (Amount₁ × Months₁) + (Amount₂ × Months₂).
